blueprint.title: Agentic Core — Reference Architecture
blueprint.positioning: Agentic Core explores a systems-engineering approach to governed Agentic AI Workflow Engineering Automation.

nodes.name: User / Business Requirement
nodes.responsibility: Define the business objective and approve a specific contract revision.
nodes.problem: Unowned objectives and ambiguous authority would enter engineering.
nodes.inputs: Business need; constraints; authorised stakeholder identity.
nodes.outputs: Requirement R; answers; approval bound to contract digest.
nodes.authority: May approve within organisational authority; cannot bypass system policy or fabricate evidence.
nodes.state: Own requirement and approval decision; no internal execution mutation.
nodes.failure: Missing or unauthorised approval leaves the contract unapproved.
nodes.scaling: External actor; asynchronous input boundary.
nodes.cloud: Identity verification; accessible input channel; approval record signing.
nodes.rule: Approval binds identity + contract version + digest; a requirement alone is not permission.

nodes.name: Requirements & Contract Engine
nodes.responsibility: Convert requirements into a versioned, reviewable engineering contract.
nodes.problem: Ambiguity would become untestable deliverables or excessive permissions.
nodes.inputs: Requirement; policy limits; clarification; stakeholder approval.
nodes.outputs: Approved versioned contract: invariants, permissions, budgets, acceptance criteria and evidence obligations.
nodes.authority: May propose terms and request clarification; cannot self-approve or widen user authority.
nodes.state: Draft/revision lifecycle; contract digest; approval identity and timestamp.
nodes.failure: Reject inconsistent constraints; invalidate prior approval when the contract changes.
nodes.scaling: Stateful per-contract aggregate; parallel drafts across isolated projects.
nodes.cloud: Document storage; schema validation; identity/authorisation; approval workflow.
nodes.rule: ApprovedCurrent := approval.digest = contract.digest ∧ approval.version = contract.version ∧ approver authorised.

nodes.name: Core Control Plane
nodes.responsibility: Own trusted run state, guarded transitions, dispatch and authority checks.
nodes.problem: Workers could bypass approval, race transitions or release unsupported artifacts.
nodes.inputs: Approved contract; plan; capability bindings; evidence; failure events.
nodes.outputs: Scoped dispatch; state transitions; repair decisions; release authority.
nodes.authority: Sole authority for run-state transitions; cannot waive the contract, policy or evidence obligations.
nodes.state: Per-run phase, pinned versions, ownership, dependency revisions, retry counters and reservations. Session-local without Memory.
nodes.failure: Fail closed on stale state, missing authority or conflicting transitions; fence outdated work.
nodes.scaling: Shared logical control plane, sharded by run; serialize mutations within each run.
nodes.cloud: Conditional state updates; workflow orchestration; authorisation; audit events.
nodes.rule: Dispatch(t) ⇒ ApprovedCurrent ∧ DependencyReady(t) ∧ Bound(t) ∧ BudgetAdmitted(t).

nodes.name: Orchestration & Planning Engine
nodes.responsibility: Decompose the contract into a dependency DAG with one accountable owner per work unit.
nodes.problem: Tasks would lack owners, readiness conditions and clear interfaces.
nodes.inputs: Current contract and planning mandate.
nodes.outputs: Versioned plan: DAG, task contracts, owners, capability needs, limits.
nodes.authority: May propose decomposition and coordination; cannot dispatch outside Core authority or approve its own outputs.
nodes.state: Plan revisions, dependency graph, owner assignments; read current contract.
nodes.failure: Reject cycles, orphan tasks and missing ownership; request clarification for infeasible work.
nodes.scaling: Planning compute can scale across runs; plans accepted atomically per revision.
nodes.cloud: Model inference; graph validation; versioned document storage.
nodes.rule: DependencyReady(t) ⇔ ∀d ∈ deps(t), AcceptedCurrent(d); |owners(t)| = 1.

nodes.name: PIC Kernel
nodes.responsibility: Select, specialise and check Pattern Inheritance & Conformance obligations for the planned domain workflow.
nodes.problem: Generated workflows could appear plausible while silently omitting governing engineering rules.
nodes.inputs: Approved plan; requirement R; versioned pattern library K; policy-required patterns.
nodes.outputs: K_R, workflow specification and trace obligations: parent pattern → child component → guard → test → evidence.
nodes.authority: May constrain specialisation and reject nonconformance; cannot approve business requirements or grant permissions.
nodes.state: Pattern library version; selected patterns; mapping and conformance schema; immutable run pin.
nodes.failure: Block missing bindings, unenforced guards or unverifiable required patterns; request a revised plan.
nodes.scaling: Versioned registry plus deterministic checking; specialisation compute scales across runs.
nodes.cloud: Versioned registry; schema/graph validation; isolated evaluation; evidence storage.
nodes.rule: Required(R,policy) ⊆ K_R ⊆ K. Each required pattern needs a current, passing trace; selection cannot remove mandatory policy.

nodes.name: Capability & Skill Registry
nodes.responsibility: Bind each planned task to compatible, qualified capability versions.
nodes.problem: Tasks could run with missing skills or incompatible interfaces.
nodes.inputs: Task capability requirements; PIC constraints; registry metadata.
nodes.outputs: Pinned capability bindings or an explicit capability gap.
nodes.authority: May select eligible bindings; cannot infer permission from availability or create unrestricted infrastructure.
nodes.state: Capability versions, qualifications, interface schemas and compatibility constraints.
nodes.failure: Unmatched requirement blocks dispatch; request approved adapter work or revise scope.
nodes.scaling: Read-heavy versioned registry; horizontally scalable lookup.
nodes.cloud: Search/index; version registry; compatibility validation; identity controls.
nodes.rule: Bound(t) ⇒ requiredCapabilities(t) ⊆ capabilities(binding(t)) ∧ Compatible(binding(t),spec).

nodes.name: Execution Layer
nodes.responsibility: Perform bounded sequential or parallel work and emit artifacts with provenance.
nodes.problem: A plan would have no implementation; unchecked workers could introduce untracked side effects.
nodes.inputs: Core dispatch; task spec; pinned capability; dependency artifacts.
nodes.outputs: Candidate artifacts; digests; task evidence; failures and measured resource use. Owner decisions arrive independently through Core.
nodes.authority: May act only within scoped dispatch; cannot mark its output accepted or self-release.
nodes.state: Task attempt; local workspace; immutable run and artifact identifiers.
nodes.failure: Timeout or invalid output goes to verification/Core; bounded retry only after admission.
nodes.scaling: Isolated worker pool; scale subject to dependency readiness and aggregate budgets.
nodes.cloud: Distributed compute; model inference; sandboxing; artifact/object storage; metering.
nodes.rule: P_task = P_run ∩ P_local; therefore P_task ⊆ P_run. Availability of a tool grants no authority.

nodes.name: Verification & Evidence Layer
nodes.responsibility: Check candidate outputs, provenance and required tests against the current task contract.
nodes.problem: Stale or untested artifacts could propagate into integration.
nodes.inputs: Artifact digest; dependency revisions; tests; owner decision; PIC obligations.
nodes.outputs: Current acceptance/rejection records; evidence bundle; bounded repair request.
nodes.authority: May reject and attest; cannot change contracts, waive required tests or grant release.
nodes.state: Acceptance records keyed by run, contract, task and artifact digest.
nodes.failure: Reject absent, stale, failed or unverifiable evidence; Core decides repair or stop.
nodes.scaling: Isolated validator pool; evidence index partitions by run.
nodes.cloud: Test runners; provenance validation; immutable evidence store; audit logging.
nodes.rule: AcceptedCurrent(t) := ownerAccepted(t) ∧ testsPass(t) ∧ report.subjectArtifactDigest = artifactDigest ∧ dependenciesCurrent(t).

nodes.name: Integration Engine
nodes.responsibility: Compose accepted components and resolve interface contracts into a candidate workflow.
nodes.problem: Individually valid pieces might not form a coherent executable system.
nodes.inputs: Accepted current components; schemas; PIC workflow specification.
nodes.outputs: Integrated candidate digest; interface checks; composition manifest.
nodes.authority: May compose accepted inputs; cannot silently modify accepted artifacts or bypass full validation.
nodes.state: Composition manifest; input digests; resulting candidate version.
nodes.failure: Interface mismatch blocks integration; changed artifacts invalidate dependent acceptance.
nodes.scaling: Isolated per-candidate build; parallelise independent assemblies.
nodes.cloud: Artifact storage; build workers; schema validation; provenance tracking.
nodes.rule: IntegrationReady ⇔ ∀t required by manifest, AcceptedCurrent(t); integration still needs end-to-end tests.

nodes.name: Final Validation & Release Gate
nodes.responsibility: Validate the integrated system against the approved contract and PIC obligations.
nodes.problem: Local task success would be confused with whole-system correctness.
nodes.inputs: Candidate; contract; acceptance records; PIC traces; current evidence.
nodes.outputs: Final attestation bound to candidate digest or a blocking defect report.
nodes.authority: May attest or block; cannot publish or authorise effects outside approved scope.
nodes.state: Final test results; candidate digest; conformance decision.
nodes.failure: Any missing guard, stale artifact or failed acceptance test blocks release.
nodes.scaling: Independent validation workers; attestation committed atomically.
nodes.cloud: System test execution; policy validation; attestation signing; audit logging.
nodes.rule: FinalPass ⇒ contractTestsPass ∧ interfacesPass ∧ PICConformance ∧ EvidenceCurrent.

nodes.name: Release Controller
nodes.responsibility: Atomically record authority and release intent for the exact attested package, then deliver with idempotency and receipt reconciliation.
nodes.problem: Validation could be separated from what is actually delivered; release races could leak invalid builds.
nodes.inputs: Current final attestation; Core authority; package digest; destination scope.
nodes.outputs: Immutable released workflow package and receipt, or blocked handoff.
nodes.authority: May release only the attested digest under current approval; deployment is a separate scoped action.
nodes.state: Release idempotency key; current attestation; receipt; phase transition.
nodes.failure: Recheck guards atomically; reject digest mismatch or revoked authority; do not claim success on unknown receipt.
nodes.scaling: Stateful idempotent release boundary; partition by run/package.
nodes.cloud: Conditional updates; artifact distribution; identity; audit receipt.
nodes.rule: Released ⇒ ApprovedCurrent ∧ OwnersAccepted ∧ FinalPass ∧ PICConformance ∧ EvidenceCurrent ∧ ReleaseAuthorised.

nodes.name: MOA Workflow
nodes.responsibility: Receive a domain-specific workflow with inherited guards, tests and an operating contract.
nodes.problem: The output would be an untraceable artifact rather than an inspectable governed workflow.
nodes.inputs: Released package, deployment-neutral configuration, PIC trace manifest.
nodes.outputs: Domain outcomes when separately executed under its operating authority.
nodes.authority: Uses only its delegated scope; is not a new unrestricted engineering system.
nodes.state: Pinned workflow version; domain run state; continuity only if Memory is enabled and bound.
nodes.failure: Unbound required modules or guards make the package nonconformant; execution effects need separate authority.
nodes.scaling: Domain-dependent single worker or multiple workers; capacity must be measured.
nodes.cloud: Workflow execution; domain adapters; identity; observability; optional durable state.
nodes.rule: P_child = P_parent ∩ P_domain. Single-worker and multi-worker specialisations preserve required guards, not identical topology.

nodes.name: Scoped Memory Controller
nodes.responsibility: Coordinate authorised record writes and context reads across run boundaries.
nodes.problem: A restarted run would lose approved facts and checkpoints, or retrieve unrelated data.
nodes.inputs: Scoped records; retrieval requests; signed context identity.
nodes.outputs: Scoped write/retrieval operations; continuity binding.
nodes.authority: May enforce retention and scope; cannot convert recalled text into permission.
nodes.state: Tenant/project/run scopes; retention policy; references to durable records.
nodes.failure: Scope mismatch blocks access; unavailable store pauses continuity-dependent work.
nodes.scaling: Stateful policy coordinator; partition by tenant/project.
nodes.cloud: Authorisation; retention policy; durable key/value storage.
nodes.rule: Retrieved ⊆ AuthorisedScope(identity,project,purpose). Memory content never enlarges P_run.

nodes.name: Durable State Store
nodes.responsibility: Persist versioned records and checkpoints with atomic write semantics.
nodes.problem: Restoration could use lost, corrupted or partially committed state.
nodes.inputs: Validated writes; scoped read requests; checkpoint manifests.
nodes.outputs: Versioned records; durable acknowledgements; integrity metadata.
nodes.authority: Execute only a currently authorised storage operation; cannot decide workflow acceptance. Checkpoint operations inherit the controller-validated access context.
nodes.state: Contracts; run checkpoints; evidence references; provenance; retention/deletion markers.
nodes.failure: Missing durable acknowledgement leaves persistence unconfirmed; reconcile the exact operation and version before retrying.
nodes.scaling: Persistent partitioned store; consistency required within each run.
nodes.cloud: Durable storage; conditional writes; encryption; backup/restore.
nodes.rule: CheckpointCommit ⇒ all referenced digests exist ∧ state version matches expected revision.

nodes.name: Provenance & Scope Enforcement
nodes.responsibility: Validate record source, purpose, identity and allowed use before memory access.
nodes.problem: Cross-project leakage and untrusted records could contaminate decisions.
nodes.inputs: Scoped access request; record provenance; current policy.
nodes.outputs: Authorised read/write decision with reason and narrowed scope.
nodes.authority: May deny or narrow access; cannot grant unavailable parent privileges.
nodes.state: Current access policy; provenance chain; retention validity.
nodes.failure: Missing provenance or policy denies access; expired records are excluded.
nodes.scaling: Stateless policy evaluator with versioned policy reads.
nodes.cloud: Identity/authorisation; provenance validation; audit logging.
nodes.rule: P_memory = P_identity ∩ P_project ∩ P_purpose; recalled approval is revalidated against current policy.

nodes.name: Retrieval Interface
nodes.responsibility: Retrieve relevant authorised history with source references for current context.
nodes.problem: Past evidence would be unavailable or mistaken for current truth.
nodes.inputs: Authorised query; scoped store results; freshness constraints.
nodes.outputs: Context bundle with provenance, timestamps, versions and confidence limits.
nodes.authority: May rank and filter permitted records; cannot approve tasks or invent facts.
nodes.state: Read index and scoped record versions; no mutation of approval state.
nodes.failure: No relevant result returns an explicit empty context; stale evidence is labelled, never reused as current acceptance.
nodes.scaling: Read-scalable retrieval service; isolated indexes.
nodes.cloud: Search/index; scoped retrieval; provenance filtering.
nodes.rule: Current evidence must match current artifact/contract digests; relevant history is not current acceptance.

nodes.name: Checkpoint & Restoration Interface
nodes.responsibility: Commit consistent run snapshots and restore only after authority and version revalidation.
nodes.problem: Recovery could replay outdated dispatch or resume against a changed contract.
nodes.inputs: Core snapshot; durable manifest; restoration request.
nodes.outputs: Verified restored state proposal for Core, or reconciliation request.
nodes.authority: May propose restored state; Core revalidates before further effects.
nodes.state: Checkpoint sequence, version pins, evidence references and restoration epoch.
nodes.failure: Resumption is blocked by a digest mismatch, obsolete authority or absent artifacts.
nodes.scaling: Per-run stateful checkpoint coordinator.
nodes.cloud: Durable snapshots; integrity checks; conditional state updates.
nodes.rule: Resume ⇒ checkpointValid ∧ pinsAvailable ∧ authorityCurrent; restoration alone permits no effect.

nodes.name: Outcome Capture
nodes.responsibility: Collect domain and engineering outcomes with provenance and consent.
nodes.problem: Improvements would be based on anecdotes or untraceable telemetry.
nodes.inputs: Workflow outcomes; verification signals; permitted metrics.
nodes.outputs: Version-attributed outcome dataset.
nodes.authority: May record allowed observations; cannot alter a run.
nodes.state: Outcome events indexed by originating version. Session-local without Memory; export is possible but cross-session durability is not assumed.
nodes.failure: Missing denominators or provenance excludes observations from evaluation.
nodes.scaling: Append-only event ingestion; scale by partition.
nodes.cloud: Event routing; metrics; audit; permitted data retention.
nodes.rule: Outcome.version = originatingRun.version; correlation does not establish causation.

nodes.name: Candidate Improvement
nodes.responsibility: Propose a bounded change to a pattern, policy or capability configuration.
nodes.problem: Lessons would become unreviewed production edits.
nodes.inputs: Attributed outcomes; baseline version; improvement hypothesis.
nodes.outputs: Candidate diff, rationale, risk scope and evaluation plan.
nodes.authority: May propose changes only; cannot promote or mutate active versions.
nodes.state: Candidate version; baseline; target scope. Session-local without Memory; export is possible but cross-session durability is not assumed.
nodes.failure: Advancement is blocked by an unclear mechanism or insufficient observations.
nodes.scaling: Stateless analysis jobs with versioned outputs.
nodes.cloud: Analysis compute; model inference; versioned artifact storage.
nodes.rule: candidate ≠ activeVersion; safety constraints remain mandatory.

nodes.name: Evaluation
nodes.responsibility: Evaluate the candidate on held-out domain cases, invariant checks and regressions.
nodes.problem: A local metric gain could hide regressions or unsafe behaviour.
nodes.inputs: Candidate; baseline; evaluation protocol; held-out cases.
nodes.outputs: Version-bound evaluation report including uncertainty and limitations.
nodes.authority: May pass/fail protocol criteria; cannot authorize promotion.
nodes.state: Dataset/protocol version; candidate digest; baseline results. Session-local without Memory; export is possible but cross-session durability is not assumed.
nodes.failure: Leakage, weak sample size or safety failure rejects promotion evidence.
nodes.scaling: Isolated parallel evaluation workers.
nodes.cloud: Test compute; dataset versioning; metrics; isolated execution.
nodes.rule: Eligible := invariantTestsPass ∧ regressionTestsPass ∧ protocolDecisionPass; empirical gains apply only to the evaluated distribution.

nodes.name: Authorised Promotion Gate
nodes.responsibility: Admit an evaluated, authorised candidate as an eligible future version.
nodes.problem: Unreviewed changes could silently rewrite current executions.
nodes.inputs: Current evaluation report; approver authority; candidate digest.
nodes.outputs: Signed promotion event for a future version.
nodes.authority: May promote within approved change scope; cannot rewrite existing run pins.
nodes.state: Approval binding; evaluation digest; promotion event. Session-local without Memory; export is possible but cross-session durability is not assumed.
nodes.failure: Stale report, revoked authority or failed conformance blocks promotion.
nodes.scaling: Serialized version-state transition; horizontally scaled requests with atomic commit.
nodes.cloud: Authorisation; conditional writes; audit log.
nodes.rule: Promote(v) ⇒ Evaluated(v) ∧ Conformant(v) ∧ Authorised(v).

nodes.name: Version Registry
nodes.responsibility: Publish immutable eligible versions and bind new runs to an explicit version set.
nodes.problem: A run might mix patterns or capabilities from incompatible versions.
nodes.inputs: Promotion or rollback selection; new-run version request.
nodes.outputs: Immutable version set and new-run pin.
nodes.authority: May select eligible versions for new runs; cannot retarget active pins.
nodes.state: Version metadata; eligible pointer; immutable pattern and capability digests. Session-local without Memory; export is possible but cross-session durability is not assumed.
nodes.failure: Unknown or revoked version blocks new-run admission; existing runs follow explicit suspension policy.
nodes.scaling: Read-heavy registry with atomic eligible-pointer writes.
nodes.cloud: Version registry; object storage; conditional updates.
nodes.rule: For active run r: pin(r,t+1) = pin(r,t). New-run selection may change.

nodes.name: Rollback Controller
nodes.responsibility: Restore the future-run default to an earlier eligible version after monitored regression.
nodes.problem: A bad promotion would remain the default without a safe reversal path.
nodes.inputs: Regression alert; rollback authority; known-good version.
nodes.outputs: Audited selection of a prior eligible version for future runs.
nodes.authority: May change future selection; current runs require an explicit suspend/restart decision by Core.
nodes.state: Rollback record; known-good version; default selector. Session-local without Memory; export is possible but cross-session durability is not assumed.
nodes.failure: Missing compatible prior version requires pause, not guessed rollback.
nodes.scaling: Small stateful control component.
nodes.cloud: Monitoring; authorisation; conditional version selection.
nodes.rule: Rollback changes defaultVersion, not immutable run pins or historical evidence.

nodes.name: Capability Requirement
nodes.responsibility: Describe a missing tool capability as an explicit engineering requirement.
nodes.problem: Missing integrations would invite unreviewed tool creation.
nodes.inputs: Unmatched task capability and allowed scope.
nodes.outputs: Adapter requirement and acceptance tests.
nodes.authority: May request an adapter; cannot provision external authority.
nodes.state: Gap record; schema and risk classification.
nodes.failure: Unapproved capability remains blocked; revise plan or seek scoped approval.
nodes.scaling: Stateless classification with versioned requirement records.
nodes.cloud: Schema registry; requirement tracking.
nodes.rule: Missing capability ⇒ block affected dispatch until an eligible binding exists.

nodes.name: Tool / Adapter Registry
nodes.responsibility: Register reviewed adapter versions, effect schemas and qualification results.
nodes.problem: Unknown tools could bypass lifecycle and compatibility controls.
nodes.inputs: Approved adapter package and test evidence; requirement.
nodes.outputs: Eligible versioned adapter binding.
nodes.authority: May expose qualified adapters; availability does not authorize use.
nodes.state: Adapter digest; schema; allowed effects; qualification evidence.
nodes.failure: Unqualified, stale or incompatible adapters are ineligible.
nodes.scaling: Read-scalable versioned registry.
nodes.cloud: Artifact registry; schema validation; qualification pipelines.
nodes.rule: Eligible(adapter) ⇒ qualificationCurrent ∧ schemaCompatible.

nodes.name: Permission Boundary
nodes.responsibility: Narrow invocation authority using run scope, task scope and adapter policy.
nodes.problem: A qualified adapter might be used with excessive access.
nodes.inputs: Invocation request; identity; parent scope; adapter effect declaration.
nodes.outputs: Expiring, effect-scoped invocation capability or denial.
nodes.authority: May deny/narrow; cannot expand parent permissions.
nodes.state: Current policy and revocations; issued capability identifier.
nodes.failure: Unknown effect or missing authority denies execution.
nodes.scaling: Stateless policy gateway with strongly current revocation reads.
nodes.cloud: Identity; authorisation; secrets brokering; audit.
nodes.rule: P_effect = P_run ∩ P_task ∩ P_adapter ∩ P_resource.

nodes.name: Execution Gateway
nodes.responsibility: Enforce bounded external effects through approved adapters.
nodes.problem: Workers could bypass reviewed tools or duplicate external effects.
nodes.inputs: Scoped capability; pinned adapter; effect request; idempotency key.
nodes.outputs: Effect receipt, measured use or explicit uncertain outcome.
nodes.authority: May invoke only admitted effects; cannot reinterpret a timeout as success.
nodes.state: Invocation key; result receipt; budget reservation; revocation state.
nodes.failure: Timeout yields unknown effect; reconcile before retry to avoid duplication.
nodes.scaling: Horizontally scalable gateway; idempotent record per effect.
nodes.cloud: Adapter execution; secrets management; rate limits; audit; metering.
nodes.rule: AllowedEffect ⇒ capabilityValid ∧ budgetReserved ∧ effectSchemaValid.

nodes.name: Effect Validation
nodes.responsibility: Validate observed side effects against the requested effect and task evidence.
nodes.problem: A successful API response could be confused with a correct business outcome.
nodes.inputs: Effect receipt; requested schema; observed downstream state.
nodes.outputs: Effect attestation or reconciliation/repair request.
nodes.authority: May attest or reject effects; cannot grant new effects.
nodes.state: Receipt digest; observation time; reconciliation status.
nodes.failure: Unknown effect remains unresolved; unsafe automatic retry is blocked.
nodes.scaling: Validator pool with domain-specific reads.
nodes.cloud: Read-back adapters; schema validation; evidence storage.
nodes.rule: EffectAccepted ⇒ observedEffect satisfies requestedPostcondition; receipt alone may be insufficient.

nodes.name: Admission & Scheduling
nodes.responsibility: Admit runnable work under global capacity, per-run limits and fairness policy.
nodes.problem: Parallel tasks could each obey local limits while exceeding the shared budget.
nodes.inputs: Ready tasks; resource estimates; current reservations.
nodes.outputs: Admitted lease requests or queued work.
nodes.authority: May delay/deny admission; cannot override dependency or authority checks.
nodes.state: Queue; reservations; per-run/tenant budgets.
nodes.failure: Overload queues or rejects explicitly; never promises unbounded throughput.
nodes.scaling: Partitioned queue; atomic shared-budget accounting.
nodes.cloud: Durable queue if continuity is required; metering; conditional reservations.
nodes.rule: spent + Σreserved + requested ≤ budget; λ < cμ is necessary in a simple homogeneous steady-state model, not a throughput guarantee.

nodes.name: Lease & Fencing Manager
nodes.responsibility: Issue attempt leases and monotonic fencing tokens for admitted workers.
nodes.problem: A timed-out worker could commit after a replacement attempt.
nodes.inputs: Admitted task; lease request; heartbeat/expiry.
nodes.outputs: Lease token; revocation; active-attempt identity.
nodes.authority: May fence attempts; cannot accept their output.
nodes.state: Lease epoch; expiry; active token.
nodes.failure: Expired workers cannot commit; receipt reconciliation still needed for external effects.
nodes.scaling: Stateful per-task coordinator; shards across tasks.
nodes.cloud: Conditional state; timers; monotonic token generation.
nodes.rule: CommitAllowed ⇔ token = currentFence ∧ leaseValid; external adapters must also enforce fencing/idempotency.

nodes.name: Bounded Repair Controller
nodes.responsibility: Convert failures into bounded repair, reconciliation, escalation or termination.
nodes.problem: Retry storms and infinite repair loops could consume all resources.
nodes.inputs: Core failure classification; attempt count; remaining budget.
nodes.outputs: Admissible repair proposal or terminal failure report.
nodes.authority: May propose retries within policy; Core remains dispatcher.
nodes.state: Retry count; deadline; failure category.
nodes.failure: Exhaustion terminates or escalates; ambiguous side effects require reconciliation.
nodes.scaling: Stateless decision workers; counters atomically owned by Core.
nodes.cloud: Failure policy evaluation; timers; audit.
nodes.rule: 0 ≤ retries(t) ≤ limit(t); finite retry limits do not alone prove termination of arbitrary worker code.

nodes.name: Observability & Capacity
nodes.responsibility: Measure latency, utilisation, failures and queueing without granting control authority.
nodes.problem: Capacity claims and recovery decisions would lack operational evidence.
nodes.inputs: Core/task events; timestamps; resource use; reconciliation results.
nodes.outputs: Metrics, alerts and capacity evidence.
nodes.authority: May alert; cannot directly alter run state or permissions.
nodes.state: Metrics windows; traces; alert rules.
nodes.failure: Missing telemetry reduces confidence and can trigger a policy-defined admission pause.
nodes.scaling: Horizontally scalable telemetry pipeline.
nodes.cloud: Event routing; metrics; distributed tracing; audit logging.
nodes.rule: Measure bottleneck capacity and tail latency; queue stability requires bounded workload assumptions.

nodes.name: Domain Specification Specialists
nodes.responsibility: Supply domain constraints and acceptance scenarios as reviewable planning advice.
nodes.problem: General decomposition could miss essential business constraints.
nodes.inputs: Contract and domain questions.
nodes.outputs: Proposed constraints, scenarios and citations for plan review.
nodes.authority: Advisory only; cannot change the approved contract.
nodes.state: Task-local analysis and cited domain evidence.
nodes.failure: Conflicting findings return to contract/plan review.
nodes.scaling: Stateless qualified worker pool.
nodes.cloud: Model inference; scoped knowledge retrieval; evidence capture.
nodes.rule: Advice becomes binding only through approved contract/plan revision.

nodes.name: Construction Specialists
nodes.responsibility: Build domain components under the Execution Layer task boundary.
nodes.problem: Specialised construction work would lack qualified implementation capacity.
nodes.inputs: Scoped construction subtask; schemas; dependency artifacts.
nodes.outputs: Component candidate with tests and provenance.
nodes.authority: Limited to task authority; cannot accept its own result.
nodes.state: Attempt-local workspace; candidate artifacts.
nodes.failure: Failure returns to Execution and verification; no independent release.
nodes.scaling: Worker pool partitioned by skill and isolation requirements.
nodes.cloud: Build compute; model inference; artifact storage; sandboxing.
nodes.rule: One accountable task owner may coordinate many workers; worker count is not architectural correctness.

nodes.name: Assurance Specialists
nodes.responsibility: Perform independent adversarial, security or domain validation where required.
nodes.problem: Specialised failure modes may escape generic tests.
nodes.inputs: Candidate, contract, risk-scoped test brief.
nodes.outputs: Reproducible findings and attestation evidence.
nodes.authority: May report failures; final acceptance remains governed by Verification.
nodes.state: Test cases; candidate digest; evidence.
nodes.failure: Unresolved critical finding blocks relevant acceptance.
nodes.scaling: Isolated validator pools; independent from construction for required risks.
nodes.cloud: Test compute; sandboxing; evidence store.
nodes.rule: Validator independence is a policy requirement for specified risks, not a claim of perfect detection.

edges.name: Submit requirement
edges.payload: Objective, constraints, success definition and stakeholder identity.
edges.purpose: Submit requirement; Draft contract is created; execution remains prohibited.
edges.pre: Identified input source.
edges.post: Draft contract is created; execution remains prohibited.
edges.failure: Ambiguous scope creates clarification request.
edges.authority: No new authority; receiver rechecks current scope.
edges.stateDependency: Identified input source.
edges.rule: The receiver validates the payload and its version before applying the stated postcondition.

edges.name: Review contract
edges.payload: Exact contract revision, digest and unresolved questions.
edges.purpose: Review contract; User can approve or request revision.
edges.pre: Draft passes consistency checks.
edges.post: User can approve or request revision.
edges.failure: No response leaves contract unapproved.
edges.authority: No new authority; receiver rechecks current scope.
edges.stateDependency: Draft passes consistency checks.
edges.rule: The receiver validates the payload and its version before applying the stated postcondition.

edges.name: Approve current contract
edges.payload: Approval identity, scope, version and digest.
edges.purpose: Approve current contract; Approval is bound to exactly one contract revision.
edges.pre: Approver is authorised; revision is current.
edges.post: Approval is bound to exactly one contract revision.
edges.failure: Stale or unauthorised approval is rejected.
edges.authority: Authorises only the specified contract scope.
edges.stateDependency: Approver is authorised; revision is current.
edges.rule: ApprovedCurrent requires exact version and digest match.

edges.name: Admit approved contract
edges.payload: Approved contract, approval proof, limits and acceptance criteria.
edges.purpose: Admit approved contract; Core creates a session run with immutable contract pin.
edges.pre: ApprovedCurrent and policy-compatible contract.
edges.post: Core creates a session run with immutable contract pin.
edges.failure: Invalid approval prevents admission.
edges.authority: Delegated run scope, narrowed by Core policy.
edges.stateDependency: ApprovedCurrent and policy-compatible contract.
edges.rule: P_run = P_approval ∩ P_policy.

edges.name: Request engineering plan
edges.payload: Contract pin, planning mandate and resource limits.
edges.purpose: Request engineering plan; Planner proposes owned dependency graph.
edges.pre: Run admitted under current policy.
edges.post: Planner proposes owned dependency graph.
edges.failure: No valid plan means no dispatch.

memory.name: Memory
memory.property: Authorised continuity across runs and sessions.
memory.off: Only in-session control state exists. Restart recovery and cross-session recall are unavailable; continuity-dependent contracts must be rejected.

learning.name: Controlled Learning
learning.property: Evaluated and authorised changes become eligible future versions; active runs keep their pins. Without Memory, this pipeline and registry are session-bound; enable Memory for persisted version history.
learning.off: No outcome-driven improvement pipeline. The selected static version remains fixed.

tools.name: Tool / Adapter Governance
tools.property: External effects pass qualified adapters, explicit permission narrowing and effect validation.
tools.off: Skeleton is restricted to sandboxed computation and artifacts. External effects requiring this boundary are not admitted.

recovery.name: Recovery & Scalability
recovery.property: Capacity admission, fencing, bounded recovery and operational measurement are explicit. Without Memory, leases, reservations and telemetry are session-local and coordinator restart requires explicit abandonment/reconciliation.
recovery.off: Basic bounded task retries remain in Core, but no distributed lease recovery or capacity-management subsystem is assumed.

specialists.name: Advanced Specialists
specialists.property: Qualified domain, construction and assurance pools augment distinct existing responsibilities.
specialists.off: Baseline capabilities perform the core work. No fixed specialist or agent count is assumed.

awsMappings.what: Cognito authenticates the stakeholder; API Gateway receives requirements. Custom Lambda validates organisational approval authority and records the exact contract digest.
awsMappings.why: Separates authenticated identity from permission to approve this business change.
awsMappings.alternative: Federate an existing enterprise identity provider through Cognito.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Identity integration does not determine business authority; organisational rules remain custom.
awsMappings.identity: Bind approver subject, tenant, role and contract revision.
awsMappings.security: Reject client-supplied role assertions; enforce resource scope server-side.
awsMappings.failure: Missing, expired or unauthorised approval leaves the contract unapproved.
awsMappings.scaling: Asynchronous submissions isolate stakeholder delays from workers.
awsMappings.protocol: Authenticated HTTPS; idempotent approval request with version and digest.
awsMappings.statefulness: Store requirement and approval records without granting internal state-write access.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: External human crosses into the trusted intake service.
awsMappings.evidence: Test altered contracts, replayed approvals and cross-tenant approvers; preserve digest-bound decisions.
awsMappings.responsibility: Define the business objective and approve a specific contract revision.
awsMappings.authority: May approve within organisational authority; cannot bypass system policy or fabricate evidence.
awsMappings.rule: Approval binds identity + contract version + digest; a requirement alone is not permission.

awsMappings.what: Lambda validates contract schemas; DynamoDB tracks revisions and approvals; versioned S3 stores contract documents. Review workflow is custom.
awsMappings.why: Makes invariants, budgets, permissions and acceptance obligations inspectable before engineering.
awsMappings.alternative: Use containerised contract validation when processing exceeds Lambda limits.
awsMappings.tradeoff: A schema-valid document can still be ambiguous; stakeholder review remains necessary.
awsMappings.identity: Separate contract proposer from authorised approver.
awsMappings.security: Approval references the immutable document digest; changes invalidate approval.
awsMappings.failure: Reject inconsistent constraints and stale approval submissions.
awsMappings.scaling: Partition revision state by tenant and contract.
awsMappings.protocol: HTTPS intake plus Step Functions task/callback integration; callbacks require identity revalidation.
awsMappings.statefulness: DynamoDB conditional updates preserve one current contract revision.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Untrusted requirements become a trusted approved contract only after checks.
awsMappings.evidence: Test revision races and digest tampering; record approved criteria and signer identity.
awsMappings.responsibility: Convert requirements into a versioned, reviewable engineering contract.
awsMappings.authority: May propose terms and request clarification; cannot self-approve or widen user authority.
awsMappings.rule: ApprovedCurrent := approval.digest = contract.digest ∧ approval.version = contract.version ∧ approver authorised.

awsMappings.what: Step Functions sequences trusted phases; Lambda implements admission predicates; DynamoDB conditional transactions own run revisions. AWS does not supply AC release logic.
awsMappings.why: Workers cannot directly dispatch themselves or change acceptance state.
awsMappings.alternative: A custom orchestrator could enforce the same predicates.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Workflow history helps auditing but does not prove business correctness.
awsMappings.identity: Dedicated controller role is the sole run-state writer.
awsMappings.security: Check current approval, dependencies, owner bindings and aggregate budget before dispatch.
awsMappings.failure: Reject stale revisions; fence cancelled or superseded attempts.
awsMappings.scaling: Partition control records by run; explicitly measure workflow and database quotas.
awsMappings.protocol: Service integrations and callback envelopes carry run, attempt, revision and digest.
awsMappings.statefulness: Baseline operational persistence supports AWS execution; optional Memory governs authorised cross-run continuity.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Trusted controller mediates every worker-to-state transition.
awsMappings.evidence: Race dispatch against revocation, stale evidence and conflicting transitions; require fail-closed results.
awsMappings.responsibility: Own trusted run state, guarded transitions, dispatch and authority checks.
awsMappings.authority: Sole authority for run-state transitions; cannot waive the contract, policy or evidence obligations.
awsMappings.rule: Dispatch(t) ⇒ ApprovedCurrent ∧ DependencyReady(t) ∧ Bound(t) ∧ BudgetAdmitted(t).

awsMappings.what: AgentCore Runtime hosts planning code; Bedrock supplies model inference. Lambda independently validates the proposed owned dependency DAG.
awsMappings.why: Reasoning produces proposals while deterministic Core admission determines executable plans.
awsMappings.alternative: Run planning in an ECS Fargate task.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Guardrails can filter model content; they cannot prove acyclicity, ownership or authority.
awsMappings.identity: Planner identity has proposal-write and contract-read access only.
awsMappings.security: No direct release, state-transition or unrestricted tool credentials.
awsMappings.failure: Cycles, missing owners or infeasible constraints return for revision.
awsMappings.scaling: Independent planning sessions scale across runs; accepted plan revision remains atomic.
awsMappings.protocol: Structured JSON proposal includes tasks, owners, dependency digests and capability needs.
awsMappings.statefulness: Versioned plan proposals in S3; Core records the admitted digest.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Probabilistic planning output crosses into deterministic plan validation.
awsMappings.evidence: Inject cycles and duplicate ownership; prove invalid plans cannot reach PIC admission.
awsMappings.responsibility: Decompose the contract into a dependency DAG with one accountable owner per work unit.
awsMappings.authority: May propose decomposition and coordination; cannot dispatch outside Core authority or approve its own outputs.
awsMappings.rule: DependencyReady(t) ⇔ ∀d ∈ deps(t), AcceptedCurrent(d); |owners(t)| = 1.

awsMappings.what: PIC is custom Lambda checking logic over an immutable versioned pattern manifest. It is not a native Bedrock feature.
awsMappings.why: Connects every required pattern to a child component, a guard, a test and current evidence.
awsMappings.alternative: Use a containerised deterministic checker for large manifests.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Schema conformance alone cannot establish that generated guards execute correctly.
awsMappings.identity: Checker reads admitted plans and pinned patterns; cannot approve requirements.
awsMappings.security: Select only within the approved library; mandatory policy patterns cannot disappear.
awsMappings.failure: Missing bindings, ineffective guards or unverifiable traces block progression.
awsMappings.scaling: Stateless checks parallelise across runs; library versions remain immutable.
awsMappings.protocol: Digest-addressed manifest and machine-readable conformance report.
awsMappings.statefulness: Core pins pattern revision; S3 preserves manifests and reports.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Generated workflow proposals cross into trusted conformance checking.
awsMappings.evidence: Remove each mandatory trace, alter guards and substitute evidence; expect explicit rejection.
awsMappings.responsibility: Select, specialise and check Pattern Inheritance & Conformance obligations for the planned domain workflow.
awsMappings.authority: May constrain specialisation and reject nonconformance; cannot approve business requirements or grant permissions.
awsMappings.rule: Required(R,policy) ⊆ K_R ⊆ K. Each required pattern needs a current, passing trace; selection cannot remove mandatory policy.

awsMappings.what: DynamoDB indexes qualified capabilities; S3 stores immutable schemas and qualification bundles. Custom Lambda resolves compatible pinned bindings.
awsMappings.why: Qualified existing skills and accountable task owners are baseline Core requirements.
awsMappings.alternative: A relational capability registry can provide equivalent version semantics.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Search convenience is secondary to complete compatibility and qualification checks.
awsMappings.identity: Registry reader selects bindings; qualification publisher has separate authority.
awsMappings.security: Tool availability never enlarges task permissions.
awsMappings.failure: Unmatched capability or expired qualification blocks affected dispatch.
awsMappings.scaling: Read-heavy lookups partition by capability and version.
awsMappings.protocol: Typed requirement-to-binding resolution returns exact schema and evidence references.
awsMappings.statefulness: Versions and qualification state persist operationally; run binding remains pinned.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Registry metadata is inspected before it can authorise a worker binding.
awsMappings.evidence: Test incompatible schemas, absent skills and revoked qualifications; capture rejected binding reasons.
awsMappings.responsibility: Bind each planned task to compatible, qualified capability versions.
awsMappings.authority: May select eligible bindings; cannot infer permission from availability or create unrestricted infrastructure.
awsMappings.rule: Bound(t) ⇒ requiredCapabilities(t) ⊆ capabilities(binding(t)) ∧ Compatible(binding(t),spec).

awsMappings.what: AgentCore Runtime hosts bounded agent work; separate Fargate tasks perform construction. Custom task wrappers emit candidate digests and provenance.
awsMappings.why: Separates model reasoning from build execution and trusted acceptance.
awsMappings.alternative: Use only Fargate workers with a model client.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Compute isolation requires explicit IAM, network and filesystem controls; managed runtime alone is insufficient.
awsMappings.identity: Per-task role and attempt identity inherit narrowed Core dispatch.
awsMappings.security: Workers cannot update acceptance records or release packages.
awsMappings.failure: Timeouts and invalid output return failures; Core admits any retry.
awsMappings.scaling: Concurrency follows ready dependencies, reservations and configured limits.
awsMappings.protocol: Signed dispatch envelope; candidate manifest and measured-use receipt.
awsMappings.statefulness: Ephemeral workspace; versioned output artifacts preserve run and attempt provenance.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Untrusted worker output enters independent verification.
awsMappings.evidence: Test forged acceptance writes, out-of-scope effects and artifact substitution; deny each escalation.
awsMappings.responsibility: Perform bounded sequential or parallel work and emit artifacts with provenance.
awsMappings.authority: May act only within scoped dispatch; cannot mark its output accepted or self-release.
awsMappings.rule: P_task = P_run ∩ P_local; therefore P_task ⊆ P_run. Availability of a tool grants no authority.

awsMappings.what: Independent Fargate test runners execute required checks; Lambda verifies owner decisions, current dependency revisions and evidence digests.
awsMappings.why: Acceptance requires both accountable owner approval and current reproducible test evidence.
awsMappings.alternative: Use CodeBuild for trusted build/test recipes with equivalent isolation.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Passing tests support stated criteria, not complete correctness of arbitrary generated code.
awsMappings.identity: Validator role differs from candidate producer and release controller.
awsMappings.security: Only controller-authorised acceptance transactions may change trusted task state.
awsMappings.failure: Reject absent owner acceptance, stale dependencies or mismatched evidence.
awsMappings.scaling: Parallel validators operate on immutable candidate versions.
awsMappings.protocol: Test report binds contract, task, attempt, artifact and dependency digests.
awsMappings.statefulness: DynamoDB acceptance index; S3 evidence bundles retain exact versions.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Candidate output crosses into independent evidence assessment.
awsMappings.evidence: Change a dependency after testing and replay an old owner decision; acceptance must fail.
awsMappings.responsibility: Check candidate outputs, provenance and required tests against the current task contract.
awsMappings.authority: May reject and attest; cannot change contracts, waive required tests or grant release.
awsMappings.rule: AcceptedCurrent(t) := ownerAccepted(t) ∧ testsPass(t) ∧ report.subjectArtifactDigest = artifactDigest ∧ dependenciesCurrent(t).

awsMappings.what: Dedicated Fargate workers compose accepted inputs. Lambda checks input acceptance references; S3 stores the resulting composition manifest.
awsMappings.why: Individual task success does not establish compatible end-to-end interfaces.
awsMappings.alternative: Use an isolated CodeBuild assembly job.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Container orchestration does not determine dependency correctness; custom digest validation is required.
awsMappings.identity: Integration role reads accepted artifacts and writes candidates only.
awsMappings.security: Prevent modification of input objects and direct release access.
awsMappings.failure: Schema mismatch or changed input invalidates dependent acceptance.
awsMappings.scaling: Parallelise independent assemblies; serialise one candidate revision commit.
awsMappings.protocol: Composition manifest enumerates exact input digests, schemas and output digest.
awsMappings.statefulness: Ephemeral build workspace; immutable assembly manifests support provenance.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Accepted components become a new unaccepted integrated candidate.
awsMappings.evidence: Inject interface incompatibility and mutate inputs; require blocked assembly or renewed verification.
awsMappings.responsibility: Compose accepted components and resolve interface contracts into a candidate workflow.
awsMappings.authority: May compose accepted inputs; cannot silently modify accepted artifacts or bypass full validation.
awsMappings.rule: IntegrationReady ⇔ ∀t required by manifest, AcceptedCurrent(t); integration still needs end-to-end tests.

awsMappings.what: Separate Fargate system tests and custom PIC checks assess the integrated candidate. A separate asymmetric KMS SIGN_VERIFY key can sign the final digest-bound attestation.
awsMappings.why: Whole-system requirements need a gate beyond local task acceptance.
awsMappings.alternative: Use a dedicated independent test account for stricter separation.
awsMappings.tradeoff: A cryptographic signature authenticates an attestation; it cannot make its assertions true.
awsMappings.identity: Final validator cannot publish or grant external effect permissions.
awsMappings.security: Bind tests, contract revision, PIC manifest and candidate digest.
awsMappings.failure: Any failed criterion, missing trace or stale evidence blocks final pass.
awsMappings.scaling: Independent candidates can validate concurrently within admitted capacity.
awsMappings.protocol: Structured final report and signature referencing immutable evidence.
awsMappings.statefulness: Immutable attestation object; Core conditionally records its current revision.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Integrated candidate crosses into final system-level assessment.
awsMappings.evidence: Remove each release prerequisite and test replay of attestations for another package.
awsMappings.responsibility: Validate the integrated system against the approved contract and PIC obligations.
awsMappings.authority: May attest or block; cannot publish or authorise effects outside approved scope.
awsMappings.rule: FinalPass ⇒ contractTestsPass ∧ interfacesPass ∧ PICConformance ∧ EvidenceCurrent.

awsMappings.what: Custom Lambda rechecks release predicates; DynamoDB atomically records authorisation and idempotency. S3 hands off the exact attested package.
awsMappings.why: Prevents a different artifact being delivered after successful validation.
awsMappings.alternative: A dedicated release service can implement equivalent guarded handoff.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Database commit and external delivery are not one transaction; reconciliation remains necessary.
awsMappings.identity: Release role has narrowly scoped package-distribution rights.
awsMappings.security: Revalidate approval, attestation, evidence, destination scope and package digest.
awsMappings.failure: Unknown delivery receipt stays unresolved; never infer success from timeout.
awsMappings.scaling: Partition idempotency records by run and package.
awsMappings.protocol: Transactional authorisation plus outbox-style delivery and authenticated receipt.
awsMappings.statefulness: Retain release intent, package version and reconciliation state operationally.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Trusted acceptance state crosses into a scoped distribution boundary.
awsMappings.evidence: Test concurrent release attempts, revoked authority and delivery retry; require one digest-bound logical handoff.
awsMappings.responsibility: Atomically record authority and release intent for the exact attested package, then deliver with idempotency and receipt reconciliation.
awsMappings.authority: May release only the attested digest under current approval; deployment is a separate scoped action.
awsMappings.rule: Released ⇒ ApprovedCurrent ∧ OwnersAccepted ∧ FinalPass ∧ PICConformance ∧ EvidenceCurrent ∧ ReleaseAuthorised.

awsMappings.what: The released MOA package may specify single-worker or multi-worker execution using these services. Its topology is domain-dependent, not predeployed.
awsMappings.why: PIC preserves required governing patterns rather than identical agent counts.
awsMappings.alternative: Execute the portable package on another qualified workflow runtime.
awsMappings.tradeoff: A valid engineering package still needs separately authorised domain execution and measured capacity.
awsMappings.identity: Child workflow receives domain-specific delegated identity and scope.
awsMappings.security: Intersect parent permission with domain permission; no implicit engineering authority.
awsMappings.failure: Missing required guards or unbound modules make execution nonconformant.
awsMappings.scaling: Measure domain workload; worker count alone proves no throughput.
awsMappings.protocol: Pinned package manifest plus typed domain adapters and operating contract.
awsMappings.statefulness: Domain operational state is separate; cross-run continuity requires an explicit Memory binding.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Engineering release crosses into separately governed domain execution.
awsMappings.evidence: Run equivalent single- and multi-worker conformance tests and attempted permission escalation.
awsMappings.responsibility: Receive a domain-specific workflow with inherited guards, tests and an operating contract.
awsMappings.authority: Uses only its delegated scope; is not a new unrestricted engineering system.
awsMappings.rule: P_child = P_parent ∩ P_domain. Single-worker and multi-worker specialisations preserve required guards, not identical topology.

awsMappings.what: Custom controller authorises cross-run records; DynamoDB and S3 hold authoritative references. Optional AgentCore Memory supports contextual recall only.
awsMappings.why: Separates governed continuity from the AWS profile’s baseline operational run persistence.
awsMappings.alternative: Use only deterministic scoped record retrieval without semantic memory.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Contextual relevance does not prove provenance, consent or current acceptance.
awsMappings.identity: Bind tenant, project, actor and declared retrieval purpose.
awsMappings.security: Memory never supplies permissions or current acceptance evidence.
awsMappings.failure: Scope mismatch denies access; continuity-dependent work pauses on store unavailability.
awsMappings.scaling: Partition authorisation and retention records by tenant/project.
awsMappings.protocol: Scoped write/read envelope returns source references and retention status.
awsMappings.statefulness: Optional cross-run retention is explicitly enabled and policy-bound.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Historical context crosses back into a current run only after scope checks.
awsMappings.evidence: Test cross-project recall, expired records and recalled approvals; require fresh authority validation.
awsMappings.responsibility: Coordinate authorised record writes and context reads across run boundaries.
awsMappings.authority: May enforce retention and scope; cannot convert recalled text into permission.
awsMappings.rule: Retrieved ⊆ AuthorisedScope(identity,project,purpose). Memory content never enlarges P_run.

awsMappings.what: DynamoDB conditional/transactional records and versioned S3 objects implement explicitly enabled continuity storage. Custom manifests coordinate multi-object commits.
awsMappings.why: Restoration needs complete, current checkpoints rather than partially persisted records.
awsMappings.alternative: Use a transactional relational store with immutable object references.
awsMappings.tradeoff: S3 versioning alone is not immutability; deny overwrites/deletion and apply suitable retention controls.
awsMappings.identity: Storage role accepts controller-validated access context only.
awsMappings.security: Encrypt scoped objects and deny cross-tenant key/resource access.
awsMappings.failure: Missing durable acknowledgement leaves persistence unconfirmed; reconcile the exact operation and version before retrying.
awsMappings.scaling: Design partition keys for checkpoint and project access patterns.
awsMappings.protocol: Conditional checkpoint commit references verified object versions and digests.
awsMappings.statefulness: Optional cross-run record lifecycle is distinct from baseline execution ledger retention.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Authorised controller request enters durable continuity storage.
awsMappings.evidence: Interrupt writes and race revisions; restoration must reject incomplete manifests and stale state.
awsMappings.responsibility: Persist versioned records and checkpoints with atomic write semantics.
awsMappings.authority: Execute only a currently authorised storage operation; cannot decide workflow acceptance. Checkpoint operations inherit the controller-validated access context.
awsMappings.rule: CheckpointCommit ⇒ all referenced digests exist ∧ state version matches expected revision.

awsMappings.what: Lambda implements provenance, purpose and retention checks; IAM limits service access. CloudTrail contributes audit records, not business authorisation decisions.
awsMappings.why: Semantic memory queries alone cannot prevent scope leakage.
awsMappings.alternative: Use a dedicated policy evaluator with equivalent provenance rules.
awsMappings.tradeoff: IAM resource permissions need custom project/purpose checks; neither replaces the other.
awsMappings.identity: Resolve authenticated principal and current organisational scope.
awsMappings.security: Compute the intersection of identity, project and purpose permissions.
awsMappings.failure: Missing source provenance, expired retention or unavailable policy denies access.
awsMappings.scaling: Stateless evaluations read pinned policy revisions.
awsMappings.protocol: Signed access context includes identity, purpose, object references and decision reason.
awsMappings.statefulness: Policy versions and provenance references persist; evaluator keeps no acceptance state.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Untrusted record claims cross into a narrow authorised access decision.
awsMappings.evidence: Test spoofed provenance and revoked permissions; verify denial before retrieval or restoration.
awsMappings.responsibility: Validate record source, purpose, identity and allowed use before memory access.
awsMappings.authority: May deny or narrow access; cannot grant unavailable parent privileges.
awsMappings.rule: P_memory = P_identity ∩ P_project ∩ P_purpose; recalled approval is revalidated against current policy.

awsMappings.what: Deterministic reads return scoped records; optional AgentCore Memory can rank contextual material. Lambda filters results and attaches provenance.
awsMappings.why: Useful history may inform reasoning without becoming current execution evidence.
awsMappings.alternative: Retrieve exact project records by key without semantic ranking.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Semantic ranking can omit relevant history; report source scope and retrieval limitations.
awsMappings.identity: Use the current run’s authorised retrieval context.
awsMappings.security: Historical approval and test reports cannot bypass fresh digest checks.
awsMappings.failure: Unavailable or unverified records return explicit omissions, never invented facts.
awsMappings.scaling: Bound query scope and result volume per request.
awsMappings.protocol: Context response contains record version, source, age and authorised purpose.
awsMappings.statefulness: No new acceptance state; context references remain traceable to retained records.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Authorised historical content enters an advisory current-run context.
awsMappings.evidence: Replay stale acceptance evidence and conflicting history; confirm no release predicate changes.
awsMappings.responsibility: Retrieve relevant authorised history with source references for current context.
awsMappings.authority: May rank and filter permitted records; cannot approve tasks or invent facts.
awsMappings.rule: Current evidence must match current artifact/contract digests; relevant history is not current acceptance.

awsMappings.what: Custom checkpoint manifests bind operational state and immutable artifacts. Lambda revalidates authority and pins before Core resumes a stopped execution.
awsMappings.why: Durable snapshots do not themselves authorise new effects.
awsMappings.alternative: Use an explicit abort-and-new-run recovery policy.
awsMappings.tradeoff: A workflow service resume facility still requires business reconciliation and current permission checks.
awsMappings.identity: Restoration role proposes state; Core retains transition authority.
awsMappings.security: Validate manifest integrity, artifact availability and current approval.
awsMappings.failure: Reject stale pins or missing references; reconcile unknown side effects.
awsMappings.scaling: Restore independently by run; serialise adoption of a snapshot.
awsMappings.protocol: Checkpoint digest, expected revision and restoration decision envelope.

awsMappings.responsibility: Commit consistent run snapshots and restore only after authority and version revalidation.

awsMappings.what: EventBridge routes outcome notifications; Lambda validates consent and lineage; S3 records observations linked to the originating run version.
awsMappings.why: Improvement analysis needs traceable observations rather than anecdotal success claims.
awsMappings.alternative: Use bounded batch ingestion from approved domain records.
