awsMappings.identity: Capture identity cannot modify active run state.
awsMappings.security: Collect only allowed fields and preserve consent/retention metadata.
awsMappings.failure: Missing lineage quarantines an observation instead of attributing it to a candidate.
awsMappings.scaling: Partition capture by project and time window.
awsMappings.protocol: Versioned event schema includes outcome, run pin, source and consent reference.
awsMappings.statefulness: Session-bound learning unless durable history is explicitly bound through Memory.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Domain observations cross into a non-authoritative learning dataset.
awsMappings.evidence: Test duplicate events, mixed version attribution and unauthorised fields; separate correlation from causation.
awsMappings.responsibility: Collect domain and engineering outcomes with provenance and consent.
awsMappings.authority: May record allowed observations; cannot alter a run.
awsMappings.rule: Outcome.version = originatingRun.version; correlation does not establish causation.

awsMappings.what: An isolated reasoning worker proposes bounded pattern or configuration changes. S3 holds candidate manifests; Guardrails provide advisory content filtering.
awsMappings.why: Exploration remains separate from promotion and active execution.
awsMappings.alternative: Generate candidates with deterministic search or human-authored changes.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Model plausibility does not establish invariant preservation or empirical improvement.
awsMappings.identity: Candidate writer cannot change defaults, trusted state or active pins.
awsMappings.security: Keep mandatory safety constraints and approved change scope immutable.
awsMappings.failure: Out-of-scope or unversioned proposals return for revision.
awsMappings.scaling: Parallel candidate generation uses independent budgets and datasets.
awsMappings.protocol: Candidate delta includes baseline version, intended change and evaluation obligations.
awsMappings.statefulness: Candidate is a distinct immutable version, never an in-place edit.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Outcome context enters a proposal-only research worker.
awsMappings.evidence: Attempt silent permission widening and direct promotion; require rejection and immutable baseline preservation.
awsMappings.responsibility: Propose a bounded change to a pattern, policy or capability configuration.
awsMappings.authority: May propose changes only; cannot promote or mutate active versions.
awsMappings.rule: candidate ≠ activeVersion; safety constraints remain mandatory.

awsMappings.what: Independent Fargate runners evaluate held-out cases and invariant regressions. Lambda assembles the protocol decision against a pinned candidate digest.
awsMappings.why: Separate measured eligibility from authorised promotion.
awsMappings.alternative: Use approved batch test infrastructure with equivalent isolation.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Empirical results apply to the evaluated distribution; they do not guarantee unseen performance.
awsMappings.identity: Evaluator may attest pass/fail but cannot publish future defaults.
awsMappings.security: Pin dataset, protocol, baseline, candidate and test harness versions.
awsMappings.failure: Missing samples, failed invariants or reproducibility failures block eligibility.
awsMappings.scaling: Parallel cases require predetermined aggregation and statistical assumptions.
awsMappings.protocol: Evaluation report includes confidence assumptions, results and provenance.
awsMappings.statefulness: Reports are versioned; cross-session learning history requires explicit retention binding.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Candidate proposals cross into independent empirical and deterministic evaluation.
awsMappings.evidence: Replay mismatched reports and introduce regression cases; preserve raw results and decision rules.
awsMappings.responsibility: Evaluate the candidate on held-out domain cases, invariant checks and regressions.
awsMappings.authority: May pass/fail protocol criteria; cannot authorize promotion.
awsMappings.rule: Eligible := invariantTestsPass ∧ regressionTestsPass ∧ protocolDecisionPass; empirical gains apply only to the evaluated distribution.

awsMappings.what: Custom Lambda checks evaluation, conformance and authorised change approval. AppConfig can distribute eligible future defaults after guarded promotion.
awsMappings.why: Passing evaluation alone cannot authorise operational change.
awsMappings.alternative: Use a manually reviewed immutable default-selection registry.
awsMappings.tradeoff: AppConfig rollout controls do not implement AC’s candidate conformance or approval predicates.
awsMappings.identity: Separate promoter role from candidate producer and evaluator.
awsMappings.security: Promotion writes future eligibility only; active pins remain unchanged.
awsMappings.failure: Digest mismatch, missing authorisation or failed protocol blocks publication.
awsMappings.scaling: Serialise promotions per configured default lineage.
awsMappings.protocol: Promotion record binds candidate, evidence, approval and prior default.
awsMappings.statefulness: Immutable eligibility records; optional durable learning history has explicit Memory scope.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Research evidence crosses into authorised future-version selection.
awsMappings.evidence: Attempt promotion without one required predicate and inspect active runs for unchanged pins.
awsMappings.responsibility: Admit an evaluated, authorised candidate as an eligible future version.
awsMappings.authority: May promote within approved change scope; cannot rewrite existing run pins.
awsMappings.rule: Promote(v) ⇒ Evaluated(v) ∧ Conformant(v) ∧ Authorised(v).

awsMappings.what: S3 manifests identify immutable eligible versions; DynamoDB binds each run to exact pins. AppConfig distributes future defaults, not live mutable run configuration.
awsMappings.why: A running workflow must remain reproducible after a new version becomes available.
awsMappings.alternative: Resolve future defaults directly from an approved registry.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Auto-refreshing configuration would violate run pinning unless defaults are resolved once at admission.
awsMappings.identity: New-run selector reads eligible versions; workers cannot retarget pins.
awsMappings.security: Validate all referenced qualifications, pattern manifests and approval scope.
awsMappings.failure: Unavailable pinned versions block start/resume rather than silently falling forward.
awsMappings.scaling: Read-heavy lookups cache immutable manifests by digest.
awsMappings.protocol: Admission resolves default into a complete explicit version-set manifest.
awsMappings.statefulness: Operational run pins persist; cross-run learned history requires explicit continuity policy.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Mutable future defaults cross into immutable per-run bindings.
awsMappings.evidence: Change AppConfig during execution; verify every active run retains its original manifest.
awsMappings.responsibility: Publish immutable eligible versions and bind new runs to an explicit version set.
awsMappings.authority: May select eligible versions for new runs; cannot retarget active pins.
awsMappings.rule: For active run r: pin(r,t+1) = pin(r,t). New-run selection may change.

awsMappings.what: CloudWatch alarms can inform AppConfig rollback of future defaults. Custom Lambda validates rollback scope and records the chosen eligible prior version. Alarm-based rollback requires configured deployment monitors; after completion, use the supported revert window or a new authorised deployment of the eligible prior default.
awsMappings.why: A monitored regression must not rewrite active workflow pins or historical evidence.
awsMappings.alternative: Use a reviewed manual future-default reset.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Automatic configuration rollback addresses monitored signals only; false alarms and unmeasured regressions remain possible.
awsMappings.identity: Rollback role controls future selection; Core controls active-run suspension.
awsMappings.security: Require earlier eligible manifests and preserve original promotion evidence.
awsMappings.failure: Unknown target eligibility blocks rollback; active defects need explicit suspend/restart decisions.
awsMappings.scaling: Coordinate one future-default lineage at a time.
awsMappings.protocol: Rollback event records reason, signal window, previous default and target digest.
awsMappings.statefulness: Future default changes; immutable run pins and audit records remain.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Monitoring observations cross into a narrowly authorised configuration decision.
awsMappings.evidence: Exercise rollback while runs execute; confirm unchanged pins and documented restart authority.
awsMappings.responsibility: Restore the future-run default to an earlier eligible version after monitored regression.
awsMappings.authority: May change future selection; current runs require an explicit suspend/restart decision by Core.
awsMappings.rule: Rollback changes defaultVersion, not immutable run pins or historical evidence.

awsMappings.what: Custom gap analysis converts missing capability bindings into a reviewable adapter engineering requirement.
awsMappings.why: An unavailable tool must block affected work instead of encouraging improvised credentials.
awsMappings.alternative: Revise scope to use an existing qualified capability.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Adapter development introduces new effects and qualification work; it is not mandatory for already-bound baseline tasks.
awsMappings.identity: Requirement proposer has no provisioning or invocation authority.
awsMappings.security: Specify effect schema and requested scope separately from permission approval.
awsMappings.failure: Unclear capability gaps return for clarification; dependent dispatch remains blocked.
awsMappings.scaling: Independent gap requests deduplicate by capability and contract scope.
awsMappings.protocol: Versioned requirement includes capability, effect limits, interfaces and acceptance tests.
awsMappings.statefulness: Persist reviewed requirements and links to blocked bindings.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Planner capability gaps cross into optional tool onboarding.
awsMappings.evidence: Request a nonexistent or excessive capability; verify no infrastructure or external permission appears automatically.
awsMappings.responsibility: Describe a missing tool capability as an explicit engineering requirement.
awsMappings.authority: May request an adapter; cannot provision external authority.
awsMappings.rule: Missing capability ⇒ block affected dispatch until an eligible binding exists.

awsMappings.what: Registry stores reviewed adapter versions and qualifications. AgentCore Gateway can expose approved adapters; custom logic binds exact adapter schema and version.
awsMappings.why: Optional onboarding adds mediated tools without replacing the Core qualified capability registry.
awsMappings.alternative: Use direct qualified adapters behind an equivalent guarded service.
awsMappings.tradeoff: A discoverable Gateway target is not automatically qualified or authorised for a task.
awsMappings.identity: Separate adapter publisher from invocation identities.
awsMappings.security: Require current qualification, resource scope and schema compatibility before binding.
awsMappings.failure: Expired qualification or incompatible schema blocks invocation.
awsMappings.scaling: Read-heavy adapter metadata supports immutable-version caching.
awsMappings.protocol: Typed adapter manifest describes requests, effects, receipts and qualification evidence.
awsMappings.statefulness: Versioned manifests and qualification records remain immutable.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Reviewed external capability metadata crosses into a permitted tool binding.
awsMappings.evidence: Test unqualified targets, changed schemas and substituted versions; verify blocked admission.
awsMappings.responsibility: Register reviewed adapter versions, effect schemas and qualification results.
awsMappings.authority: May expose qualified adapters; availability does not authorize use.
awsMappings.rule: Eligible(adapter) ⇒ qualificationCurrent ∧ schemaCompatible.

awsMappings.what: Custom invocation admission intersects AC run/task/adapter/resource scopes. AgentCore Policy in ENFORCE mode supplies an additional Gateway policy check.
awsMappings.why: Managed tool authorisation supplements rather than replaces contract, budget and artifact predicates.
awsMappings.alternative: Use a dedicated custom policy service with equivalent enforcement.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Policy authoring and credential mediation still require validated mappings and least-privilege target permissions.
awsMappings.identity: AgentCore Identity mediates credentials after authenticated scoped admission.
awsMappings.security: Compute the permission intersection; never expose broad credentials to the model.
awsMappings.failure: Missing policy context or admission record denies invocation.
awsMappings.scaling: Stateless policy checks read current versioned scope records.
awsMappings.protocol: Admitted effect envelope carries schema, budget reservation, identity and resource constraints.
awsMappings.statefulness: Decision receipt binds policy version and task attempt.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Worker request crosses into trusted external-effect authorisation.
awsMappings.evidence: Test parent-disallowed resources, revoked tokens and budget exhaustion before any target call.
awsMappings.responsibility: Narrow invocation authority using run scope, task scope and adapter policy.
awsMappings.authority: May deny/narrow; cannot expand parent permissions.
awsMappings.rule: P_effect = P_run ∩ P_task ∩ P_adapter ∩ P_resource.

awsMappings.what: Gateway exposes mediated targets; Policy ENFORCE checks tool permissions; Identity handles scoped credentials. Custom AC admission precedes every call.
awsMappings.why: External effects require a validated schema, a reserved budget and a qualified adapter binding.
awsMappings.alternative: Use a custom adapter proxy with equivalent authentication and enforcement.
awsMappings.tradeoff: A tool response or timeout does not establish that the requested effect happened exactly once.
awsMappings.identity: Target credentials remain mediated and constrained to approved resources.
awsMappings.security: Reject calls without a current admission receipt and idempotency context.
awsMappings.failure: Timeout creates an unknown outcome requiring reconciliation, not blind replay.
awsMappings.scaling: Bound target concurrency by measured limits and reservations.
awsMappings.protocol: Supported target integration plus typed request, idempotency key and effect receipt.
awsMappings.statefulness: Persist admission and effect correlation records outside worker memory.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Trusted adapter boundary crosses into external systems.
awsMappings.evidence: Simulate timeout after side effect and duplicate delivery; require reconciliation without unauthorised repetition.
awsMappings.responsibility: Enforce bounded external effects through approved adapters.
awsMappings.authority: May invoke only admitted effects; cannot reinterpret a timeout as success.
awsMappings.rule: AllowedEffect ⇒ capabilityValid ∧ budgetReserved ∧ effectSchemaValid.

awsMappings.what: Custom validators compare observed effects with requested postconditions and produce digest-bound effect evidence. DynamoDB records reconciliation status.
awsMappings.why: A transport receipt may show delivery while the business change remains incomplete.
awsMappings.alternative: Use adapter-specific independent read-back checks.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Some targets cannot expose atomic read-back; explicitly document uncertainty and escalation.
awsMappings.identity: Validator has restricted observation access, not permission for new effects.
awsMappings.security: Bind observation to task, adapter version, requested resource and idempotency key.
awsMappings.failure: Mismatch or unknown result blocks task acceptance and routes to Core.
awsMappings.scaling: Parallel read-back is limited by target quotas and consistency windows.
awsMappings.protocol: Postcondition report includes observed state, provenance and requested effect digest.
awsMappings.statefulness: Retain reconciliation outcomes and evidence versions operationally.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: External system claims cross into independent effect assessment.
awsMappings.evidence: Return misleading success receipts and delayed effects; ensure acceptance follows verified postconditions.
awsMappings.responsibility: Validate observed side effects against the requested effect and task evidence.
awsMappings.authority: May attest or reject effects; cannot grant new effects.
awsMappings.rule: EffectAccepted ⇒ observedEffect satisfies requestedPostcondition; receipt alone may be insufficient.

awsMappings.what: SQS buffers ready work; custom admission uses DynamoDB transactions to reserve capacity and aggregate budgets before Core dispatch.
awsMappings.why: Queue availability cannot bypass dependencies, permission checks or shared run limits.
awsMappings.alternative: Use Step Functions scheduling without a distributed queue for bounded workloads.
awsMappings.tradeoff: SQS redelivery and ordering require idempotent envelopes; a queue alone proves no fairness.
awsMappings.identity: Scheduler may delay/deny work; Core remains dispatcher.
awsMappings.security: Recheck current authority and dependency revisions at admission.
awsMappings.failure: Stale reservations or overload trigger conservative delay and reconciliation.
awsMappings.scaling: Measure service rates and tail latency; configure capacity rather than claiming throughput.
awsMappings.protocol: Task envelope carries run, attempt, expected revision and reservation identity.
awsMappings.statefulness: Operational reservations persist; optional recovery adds distributed scheduling semantics.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Runnable proposals cross into capacity-checked execution admission.
awsMappings.evidence: Race concurrent reservations and simulate redelivery; assert aggregate budget never exceeds its bound.
awsMappings.responsibility: Admit runnable work under global capacity, per-run limits and fairness policy.
awsMappings.authority: May delay/deny admission; cannot override dependency or authority checks.
awsMappings.rule: spent + Σreserved + requested ≤ budget; λ < cμ is necessary in a simple homogeneous steady-state model, not a throughput guarantee.

awsMappings.what: Custom lease logic conditionally advances monotonically increasing attempt epochs in DynamoDB. Workers must present current fencing tokens at commit.
awsMappings.why: A timed-out worker must not overwrite results from its replacement.
awsMappings.alternative: Use single-owner serial execution where distributed leases are unnecessary.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Lease expiration is insufficient without fencing at every protected commit and applicable adapter.
awsMappings.identity: Lease issuer cannot accept outputs; worker identity binds attempt epoch.
awsMappings.security: Restrict fence updates to trusted lease service; reject older tokens.
awsMappings.failure: Expired or mismatched lease denies commit and requires reconciliation.
awsMappings.scaling: Partition lease records by task; account for heartbeat load.
awsMappings.protocol: Lease acquire/renew/release includes expected epoch and attempt identity.
awsMappings.statefulness: Operational lease state is distinct from optional cross-run contextual Memory.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Worker claims cross into authoritative attempt ownership.
awsMappings.evidence: Pause old workers, issue replacement leases and resume them; stale commits must fail.
awsMappings.responsibility: Issue attempt leases and monotonic fencing tokens for admitted workers.
awsMappings.authority: May fence attempts; cannot accept their output.
awsMappings.rule: CommitAllowed ⇔ token = currentFence ∧ leaseValid; external adapters must also enforce fencing/idempotency.

awsMappings.what: Step Functions supports bounded retry mechanics; custom repair logic checks deadline, attempt allocation, reservations and unknown-effect reconciliation.
awsMappings.why: Repair must consume the same constrained authority and budget as original work.
awsMappings.alternative: Stop and request stakeholder intervention for nonrecoverable failures.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Finite retry count alone does not prove termination of arbitrary worker code.
awsMappings.identity: Repair controller proposes action; trusted Core alone admits dispatch.
awsMappings.security: No policy widening, stale dependency reuse or blind external-effect replay.
awsMappings.failure: Exhausted limits produce escalation or terminal failure.
awsMappings.scaling: Backoff and measured capacity prevent correlated retry storms.
awsMappings.protocol: Failure envelope classifies retryable, reconcilable and terminal outcomes.
awsMappings.statefulness: Operational attempt counters and decisions remain versioned by task.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Worker failures cross into a guarded repair decision.
awsMappings.evidence: Exhaust budgets, hang workers and duplicate failure events; assert bounded admitted retries and explicit terminal states.
awsMappings.responsibility: Convert failures into bounded repair, reconciliation, escalation or termination.
awsMappings.authority: May propose retries within policy; Core remains dispatcher.
awsMappings.rule: 0 ≤ retries(t) ≤ limit(t); finite retry limits do not alone prove termination of arbitrary worker code.

awsMappings.what: CloudWatch records approved metrics; OpenTelemetry traces requests; CloudTrail contributes API audit activity. Custom instrumentation preserves AC task and version identifiers. AgentCore Observability instruments runtime agents with CloudWatch-compatible OTEL traces and metrics.
awsMappings.why: Capacity and failure claims need measured workload evidence.
awsMappings.alternative: Use another approved OpenTelemetry-compatible collection pipeline.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Service logs do not automatically capture domain correctness or every external side effect.
awsMappings.identity: Telemetry writers cannot change permissions or run state.
awsMappings.security: Redact sensitive payloads and constrain metric/log access.
awsMappings.failure: Lost or delayed telemetry is explicit; conservative admission uses configured limits.
awsMappings.scaling: Measure queue depth, latency percentiles, utilisation and bottleneck rates.
awsMappings.protocol: Structured events correlate run, contract, attempt, artifact and service request.
awsMappings.statefulness: Operational retention differs from optional research-memory continuity.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Runtime observations cross into read-only analysis and alerts.
awsMappings.evidence: Inject telemetry loss and workload spikes; verify no fabricated capacity figures or direct authority changes.
awsMappings.responsibility: Measure latency, utilisation, failures and queueing without granting control authority.
awsMappings.authority: May alert; cannot directly alter run state or permissions.
awsMappings.rule: Measure bottleneck capacity and tail latency; queue stability requires bounded workload assumptions.

awsMappings.what: Optional AgentCore Runtime specialists provide domain constraints and acceptance scenarios using Bedrock. Their structured advice enters planning review.
awsMappings.why: Specialist knowledge enriches proposals without changing the approved contract.
awsMappings.alternative: Use qualified human specialists or deterministic domain rule libraries.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Model advice can be incomplete; evidence and stakeholder review remain necessary.
awsMappings.identity: Domain specialist identity reads scoped requirements and writes advisory outputs.
awsMappings.security: No contract approval, release authority or broad external tools.
awsMappings.failure: Unsupported advice is rejected; required changes need approved contract revision.
awsMappings.scaling: Independent domain consultations scale across runs under budget admission.
awsMappings.protocol: Advice bundle includes sources, scenarios, assumptions and intended contract impact.
awsMappings.statefulness: Session-scoped advice; accepted revisions persist through the normal contract path.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Advisory reasoning crosses into reviewed planning, never directly into authority.
awsMappings.evidence: Offer conflicting or unsupported constraints; confirm no silent contract modification.
awsMappings.responsibility: Supply domain constraints and acceptance scenarios as reviewable planning advice.
awsMappings.authority: Advisory only; cannot change the approved contract.
awsMappings.rule: Advice becomes binding only through approved contract/plan revision.

awsMappings.what: Optional isolated Fargate construction workers build domain components, invoking Bedrock only for bounded assistance. Execution retains the task boundary.
awsMappings.why: Separates build environments from trusted control and independent assurance.
awsMappings.alternative: Use qualified baseline execution capabilities without a specialist pool.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Generated code needs sandbox controls and independent tests; extra workers do not prove correctness.
awsMappings.identity: Per-task worker identity inherits scoped dispatch and one accountable owner.
awsMappings.security: Deny acceptance writes, release rights and broad egress.
awsMappings.failure: Invalid artifacts return to Execution for governed verification and repair.
awsMappings.scaling: Parallel construction follows dependency readiness and aggregate reservations.
awsMappings.protocol: Task contract plus pinned inputs; output manifest records artifact digest and provenance.
awsMappings.statefulness: Ephemeral workspaces; immutable candidate artifacts are operational records.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Construction output crosses into independent verification.
awsMappings.evidence: Test permission escalation, hidden dependencies and self-acceptance; require blocked actions.
awsMappings.responsibility: Build domain components under the Execution Layer task boundary.
awsMappings.authority: Limited to task authority; cannot accept its own result.
awsMappings.rule: One accountable task owner may coordinate many workers; worker count is not architectural correctness.

awsMappings.what: Optional separate Fargate assurance workers perform adversarial, security or domain tests. Findings return to Verification, not directly to release.
awsMappings.why: Specified risks can require independent assessment beyond the artifact producer.
awsMappings.alternative: Use qualified external reviewers with the same scoped evidence contract.
awsMappings.tradeoff: Independence improves challenge quality but cannot guarantee detection of every defect.
awsMappings.identity: Assurance identity differs from construction and has evidence-read/report-write access.
awsMappings.security: No modification of candidate artifacts, approved criteria or trusted acceptance state.
awsMappings.failure: Inconclusive findings block policy-required assurance rather than implying success.
awsMappings.scaling: Parallel risk-specific tests obey admitted budgets and isolation requirements.
awsMappings.protocol: Risk brief references candidate digest; report contains reproducible findings and test versions.
awsMappings.statefulness: Immutable findings preserve exact assessed artifact and scope.
awsMappings.trustBoundary: Independent specialist findings cross into governed Verification decisions.
awsMappings.evidence: Inject known vulnerabilities and swapped candidates; assess detection coverage and reject mismatched reports.
awsMappings.responsibility: Perform independent adversarial, security or domain validation where required.
awsMappings.authority: May report failures; final acceptance remains governed by Verification.
awsMappings.rule: Validator independence is a policy requirement for specified risks, not a claim of perfect detection.

decisions.choice: Step Functions Standard with custom deterministic admission
decisions.reason: Human approval, durable job waits and auditable transitions are required. The planner proposes an owned DAG; custom validation admits ready frontiers. Map/Parallel fan out independent admitted tasks, not arbitrary dependency graphs.
decisions.limit: Retries, callbacks and redrives still require digest guards, durable idempotency and unknown-effect reconciliation.

decisions.choice: AgentCore Runtime reasoning + separate Fargate job/assurance tasks
decisions.alternative: Everything in Lambda / one shared agent process
decisions.reason: Reasoning sessions and finite construction/testing jobs have different lifecycle and trust requirements. Lambda enforces short deterministic guards; microVM Runtime hosts reasoning; separate Fargate tasks use qualified ECR image digests.
decisions.limit: Qualified workloads only until hostile-code threat assessment is complete. Task isolation is not universal adversarial sandboxing; builders and verifiers do not share one task.

decisions.choice: Explicit custom PIC compiler and conformance checker
decisions.reason: PIC maps each required AC pattern into a child component, enforcing guard, negative test and current evidence digest. AWS supplies compute and storage; the transformation and checks must be engineered.
decisions.limit: A complete trace is necessary design evidence. It does not prove domain correctness or automatically generate correct software.

decisions.choice: DynamoDB authority ledger + versioned S3 artifacts + outbox
decisions.alternative: LLM conversation as state / store everything in one document
decisions.reason: Conditional state transitions, current owner/digest acceptance and reservation epochs need trusted structured state. Large artifacts and exact immutable manifests belong in S3; pin versionId and SHA-256.
decisions.limit: No transaction spans DynamoDB, S3 and external effects. Write/verify artifact first; commit ledger + outbox atomically; deliver idempotently and reconcile.

decisions.choice: Custom effect admission + AgentCore Gateway / Policy ENFORCE / Identity
decisions.reason: AC run/task/adapter/resource scope, budget and fence are evaluated before invocation. Gateway mediates reviewed targets; blocking policy is ENFORCE, not LOG_ONLY. Workers have no independent external-effect path.
decisions.limit: IAM policy evaluation is more complex than a set-intersection diagram. Target resource policies, session grants and external postconditions require explicit review.

decisions.choice: Optional scoped contextual Memory + exact record/checkpoint store
decisions.alternative: Use semantic recall for contracts and acceptance
decisions.reason: AgentCore Memory is evaluated only for fallible contextual history, with authorised namespaces/provenance. Exact contract, checkpoint and evidence records remain in DynamoDB/S3 under a custom controller.
decisions.limit: Memory-off rejects continuity-dependent contracts and exposes no cross-run retrieval or application restore. Managed orchestration retains operational records: this is an explicit cloud adaptation, not semantic continuity.

decisions.choice: Immutable, evaluated future versions; AppConfig only selects future defaults
decisions.alternative: Autonomous retraining / mutate active system prompts
decisions.reason: Outcome provenance, held-out evaluation, conformance and scoped approval precede promotion. Each run snapshots its complete version set; pinned Step Functions version, image digests and pattern manifests remain invariant.
decisions.limit: Learning results cover only the evaluated distribution. AppConfig rollback must be wired and authorised; active runs never follow changing defaults.

decisions.choice: One authoritative Region; bounded quotas and two-AZ job placement
decisions.reason: Serial ownership, fenced attempts and atomic authority simplify the reference implementation. Managed regional services and private job subnets provide failure separation; SQS adds backpressure when Recovery is enabled.
decisions.limit: Region/model/AgentCore feature availability, endpoints and quotas are implementation admission checks. No RTO, RPO or throughput is claimed before load and recovery measurement.

caveats: Step Functions Standard supports callbacks/job waits and exactly-once workflow execution semantics; retries, redrives and downstream uncertainty still require application idempotency/fencing. Never claim exactly-once external business effects.

Step Functions Parallel/Map are not a dynamic arbitrary-DAG scheduler. Validate DAG and dispatch ready frontiers; use Distributed Map only for independent admitted tasks with explicit MaxConcurrency and downstream capacity limits.

DynamoDB TransactWriteItems is atomic across up to 100 distinct items / 4 MB in one account and Region; its ClientRequestToken idempotency window is 10 minutes. Durable business idempotency requires persistent keys/current-state conditions.

DynamoDB ledger transactions cannot atomically write S3, invoke an external system or send a callback. Use a transactional outbox and reconcile unknown effect outcomes; external targets enforce fence/idempotency.

AgentCore Runtime microVM mode gives per-session CPU/memory/filesystem isolation. It is a session host, not the authoritative approval/evidence ledger; ephemeral state is lost when compute ends unless persistence is explicitly configured.

Fargate isolates task infrastructure; containers inside the same task share resources. Separate trust domains into separate tasks/accounts/roles, use qualified images and constrained networking, and perform a specific threat assessment for hostile generated code. Do not label Fargate an automatic adversarial sandbox.

AgentCore Gateway discovery/schema conversion is not adapter qualification. IAM/JWT authenticate callers; Policy ENFORCE and custom contextual guard enforce tool authority. LOG_ONLY is observational and must not be shown as a blocking guard.
AgentCore Identity handles workload/user-scoped credential access; credential possession does not satisfy the run contract, budget, fence, purpose or effect-postcondition checks.

AgentCore Memory long-term extraction is asynchronous; summaries/semantic records are fallible contextual data, not approved contracts, exact checkpoints, current evidence or automatic evaluated learning.

Blueprint Memory OFF rejects continuity-dependent contracts and exposes no application restore/history/retrieval. AWS managed orchestration has retained operational records; label this cloud adaptation and do not expose service persistence as enabled semantic continuity.

Bedrock Guardrails filters configurable content/grounding; Automated Reasoning checks operate detect-only and use natural-language translation with stated limits. PIC trace checking and deterministic domain/system tests remain custom.

S3 Object Lock requires Versioning and protects a particular object version; new versions/delete markers can still be created. Pin exact versionId and cryptographic content digest. Governance may be bypassed by specially authorised identities; compliance is stronger during retention. Retention is not artifact correctness.

IAM permissions boundaries are maximum identity-policy permissions, not grants; same-account resource grants to session principals have evaluation subtleties. Avoid treating application P_effect intersection as a complete description of AWS IAM evaluation.

Controlled learning uses held-out/versioned evaluation and authorised promotion. Bedrock evaluations assess finite datasets and judge models can err; no universal improvement/causal/generalisation claim. Active run pins remain invariant.
